articles.body: El Villarreal recibe al Deportivo este sábado en el Estadio de la Cerámica, en el partido correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de LaLiga 26/27, un choque en el que el submarino amarillo abre por primera vez las puertas de su estadio esta temporada tras haber disputado sus tres primeras citas fuera de casa. El conjunto de Íñigo Pérez llega con la necesidad de sumar su primera victoria. Ha empatado 2-2 tanto ante el Racing como ante el Atlético de Madrid, y cayó la pasada jornada por 1-0 en Mendizorroza ante el Alavés, lo que le deja con solo dos puntos de nueve posibles. Favorito para el partido entre Villarreal y Deportivo Por su parte, el Deportivo llega a la Cerámica como uno de los equipos revelación del arranque liguero. El conjunto gallego, que aún no conoce la derrota en su regreso a Primera, ha sumado cinco puntos gracias a los empates ante Elche y Málaga (1-1 en ambos casos) y a la victoria por 3-1 sobre el Valencia en Riazor, con Aubameyang como gran protagonista tras marcar en las tres jornadas disputadas. El club coruñés, además, ha reforzado su plantilla en el cierre de mercado con la llegada de José María Giménez, cedido por el Atlético de Madrid, y de Marc Casadó, a préstamo desde el Barcelona. Con todos estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como favorito al Villarreal, que necesita reaccionar en casa tras su irregular inicio. Betfair paga la victoria local a cuota 1.44, por 4.50 del empate y 5.50 de la victoria del conjunto gallego. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más interesantes del encuentro. El Villarreal no ha logrado dejar su portería a cero en ninguna de sus tres primeras jornadas, y el Dépor tampoco ha conseguido un partido sin encajar, pese a su condición de invicto. Con estos datos, según las apuestas deportivas, la probabilidad de que ambos equipos anoten es alta. Betfair paga a 1.88 el "sí", misma cuota del "no". Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con bastante producción ofensiva. El Villarreal ha firmado cuatro tantos en sus tres primeros partidos, mientras que el Deportivo ha marcado cinco, y ambos han encajado en cada una de sus citas ligueras. Ningún duelo de los disputados hasta ahora por los dos equipos ha terminado con menos de dos goles en total. Betfair sitúa la cuota del +2.5 totales a 1.66, por 2.15 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. El Villarreal, con un estilo de juego asociativo y ataque por bandas apoyado en Pépé y Moleiro, suele generar un volumen alto de saques de esquina cuando actúa como local. El Deportivo, por su parte, ha mostrado en sus primeras salidas un perfil más directo, con Aubameyang como principal referencia arriba, lo que en ocasiones se traduce en menos llegadas por el exterior y, por tanto, en un menor número de córners a favor propio frente a un rival que buscará dominar el balón desde el inicio. articles.title: Reds hit 3 home runs and hold on for 5-3 victory over Brewers
articles.summary: Matt McLain snapped a seventh-inning tie with a leadoff homer and the Cincinnati Reds held on to beat the Milwaukee Brewers 5-3 on Saturday night.  Elly De L...
articles.body:
CINCINNATI (AP) — Matt McLain snapped a seventh-inning tie with a leadoff homer and the Cincinnati Reds held on to beat the Milwaukee Brewers 5-3 on Saturday night.

Elly De La Cruz and Tyler Stephenson also went deep for the last-place Reds in a game delayed more than two hours by rain. Emilio Pagán pitched out of a bases-loaded jam in the ninth for his 21st save in 24 chances.

William Contreras homered early for the major league-leading Brewers (88-55), who hold a seven-game lead in the NL Central over the Chicago Cubs. Milwaukee began the day last in the big leagues with 132 home runs.

Contreras connected off Andrew Abbott in the first inning, his 14th. De La Cruz answered with his 22nd home run off Dustin May in the bottom half.

The game was delayed by rain for 2 hours, 22 minutes in the fourth. The Reds trailed 2-1 and Jose Trevino singled off DL Hall to tie the score.

Stephenson hit his 15th homer to open the sixth, but the Brewers pulled even on three straight singles against Tony Santillan. Jackson Chourio knocked in the tying run.

Santillan (3-4) struck out Contreras with the bases loaded to keep it tied.

McLain launched his 15th home run off Aaron Ashby (13-3) in the seventh. Eugenio Suárez doubled in the eighth and scored from second base on a wild pitch by Grant Anderson to make it 5-3.

Milwaukee loaded the bases against Pagán with one out in the ninth, but Luis Lara popped up and Contreras flied out to end it.

Abbott's outing was shortened by the rain delay. The 2025 All-Star has not won since Aug. 6 against the Athletics.

Carlos Jorge went 0 for 4 with two strikeouts in his first major league start in center field for Cincinnati.

Brewers LHP Kyle Harrison (10-4, 3.45 ERA) faces Reds RHP Brady Singer (5-13, 4.83) on Sunday.

articles.title: Canaries punch playoff ticket with win over Lincoln
articles.summary: SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (CANARIES) – The Sioux Falls Canaries are headed to the Miles Cup Playoffs for the fourth consecutive season and for the eighth time in fra...
articles.body:
SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (CANARIES) - The Sioux Falls Canaries are headed to the Miles Cup Playoffs for the fourth consecutive season and for the eighth time in franchise history after topping Lincoln 3-2 at the Birdcage.

The Canaries were held to one hit through the first five innings but rallied to score three runs with two outs in the bottom of the sixth. Anthony Hall broke the scoreless tie with a two-run single before Grady Mee added an RBI bunt.

The 3-0 score held until the Saltdogs fought back with a two-run homer in the top of the ninth but Charlie Hasty stuck out the next two batters and induced a groundout to end the game.

Josh Rehwaldt finished with two hits while Nicholas Arbach scattered three hits over six shutout innings and fanned five to earn the win. The Canaries (50-48) return to action Sunday at 4:05pm.

articles.title: Missouri State football honors Springfield with helmet flag decal
articles.summary: Missouri State football added the Springfield city flag to their helmets to show commitment to the local community.
articles.body:
Missouri State donned a new helmet decal during its Week 1 game against No. 8 Texas A&M on Saturday, Sept. 5.

On the front of the helmet, the City of Springfield flag is represented. The blue and white flag contrasted well with the Bears' white and Maroon helmet. The city's flag was adopted in 2022, after the Springfield Identity Project created it nearly a decade ago.

The team put the flag on the helmet as a sense of pride for the university's hometown, head coach Casey Woods said following the game to the Missouri State Radio Network.

"We put that Springfield flag on our helmet so Springfield understands how invested we are in them," Woods said. "We need their investment in us."

Missouri State hosts Lindenwood for its home opener on Saturday, Sept. 12. Woods has a goal of setting the attendance record against Lindenwood, an in-state opponent.

The record was set in 2014 against North Dakota. There were 18,386 fans in attendance for the game.

articles.title: WMU coach addresses Michigan Hail Mary, says clock 'was past zeros'
articles.summary: WMU football coach Lance Taylor, speaking to media after his team's loss to Michigan, said that when he looked up at the clocks, it was "past zeros"
articles.body:
Western Michigan coach Lance Taylor said "you can't always control" the situations that led to Michigan's controversial last-second win, but acknowledged he believed the game was over before the last second touchdown.

He told reporters postgame he hadn't seen a replay of what transpired, but that MAC commissioner Jon Steinbrecher had already reached out to Big Ten officiating about what led to a second being added to the clock after it appeared the game ended following a failed Hail Mary attempt.

The officials ruled there was still time left, leading to Bryce Underwood connecting with JJ Buchanan on a 41-yard Hail Mary touchdown for the 13-12 victory.

"At the end of the day, you don't always control those situations, or is there a second left on the clock?" Taylor said. "We talk about a lot about just respond, regardless of what the circumstances are. We can't control whether there's a second left on the clock or not. We went out the first time, we defended perfectly the Hail Mary situation.

"I thought our guys did an excellent job. I know when I looked up at the clock, it was past zeros before we touched it. I knew that they would review it. It was the last play of the game, and because we defended it so well, wasn't worried or concerned about our guys going out and defending it the second time.

Unfortunately, we did not defend it as well the second time."

Taylor complimented the officiating crew, saying they did "a really nice job handling multiple close calls and review situations." Regardless of the controversy, the Broncos coach said Michigan made a great play and it's a strong lesson for his team.

"We can't just box out the back of the end zone. We've got to make sure that we cover them up at the front line as well, so we'll learn from that and grow," he added. "For sure, I'll watch the TV copy."

articles.title: Jon Sumrall's postgame quotes after Florida throttles FAU in opener
articles.summary: SEC Network sideline reporter Taylor Davis spoke with Jon Sumrall after the conclusion of the game. Here is what was said between the two.
articles.body:
The Jon Sumrall era began with a bang inside Ben Hill Griffin on Saturday night as the Gators throttled the FAU Owls , 66-21, in a game that showcased the program's explosive new offense.

The Orange and Blue logged 624 total yards of offense — the most since 2020 — and the 66 points scored were the most in a season opener since 1988 against Montana State. Offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner deserves a heaping helping of credit for the corps' performance, thanks to a potent ground game headlined by Jadan Baugh's 160-yard effort and a steady presence under center from Aaron Philo.

SEC Network sideline reporter Taylor Davis spoke with Sumrall after the conclusion of the game. Here is what was said between the two.

PHOTOS: Highlights from Florida's season-opening win vs FAU Owls

With a lot of new pieces, you entered the year with a lot of questions. What answers did you get tonight?

I thought our offensive skill played really good. They're explosive. Still got a lot of questions on defense. We've got a lot of room to grow.

66 points, led by Aaron Philo. What did you see from him?

It was fun to watch him play. He played confident, played poised, cut it loose, made good decisions, and that one interception wasn't on him. We should have caught that ball. Really proud of him.

You told us this is your dream. Day 1, first win. What was this like?

It's fun. I enjoy coaching. Today's about the players. Saturdays, it's their day. Every other day is my day. Sunday through Friday is about us coaching them. We've got a lot of work to do to go where we want to go.

articles.title: XCEPTIONAL ATHLETE: Little Chute’s Reece Joten
articles.summary: (WFRV) – Little Chute High School senior Reece Joten is one of the key players to a senior studded Little Chute football team, and also Local 5’s Xceptional...
articles.body:
(WFRV) - Little Chute High School senior Reece Joten is one of the key players to a senior studded Little Chute football team, and also Local 5's Xceptional Athlete of the Week.

Playing both sides of the ball, as a running back and a middle linebacker, Joten has a unique skillset that he brings to his team, using his speed to not only score touchdowns, but to fly around the backfield making tackles as well.

During his junior season Joten helped lead the Mustangs to the Division 4 state championship game (where they would go on to lose 28-22 to the Winneconne Wolves). Last season, Joten averaged 8 yards per carry, had 23 touchdowns and on the defensive side, he had 98 total tackles, and 3 interceptions and this year he hopes to improve even more.

"We did good last season, but there are definitely a lot of areas to do better, and if I can just make one more tackle, or one more play than I did last year, then that's a win," Joten said.

Little Chute has 23 seniors on their roster this year, the most seniors that Head Coach Mark Krommenacker has ever had on one squad.

"When you have 23 seniors you have a chance to compete with anybody," Krommenacker said.

With that senior leadership, this Little Chute team has a good chance of making it back to the state championship again this year, especially when one of those seniors is as versatile as Joten.

This group has a unique chemistry, both on and off of the field, as they have been playing football together since fifth grade, and even some of them playing Pop Warner together in third grade before that.

So far this season, the Mustangs are already off to a hot 3-0 start, with Joten leading in both rushing yards (226), and tackles (26).

articles.title: 3 Pirates Players Must Lock In to Keep Playoff Hopes Alive
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Pirates had a terrible month in August. Their odds of making the playoffs on July 22 were about 50/50, coming in at 47.2%. A month later, on A...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Pirates had a terrible month in August. Their odds of making the playoffs on July 22 were about 50/50, coming in at 47.2%. A month later, on August 22 , their playoff odds had fallen to just 2%. However, the Pirates are making one last push to put themselves back into playoff contention. At the time of this writing, they've won five of their last six series and have put themselves 4 1/2 games out of a Wild Card spot. It's still a long shot, but the Pirates' playoff hopes are not completely dead, even if they are on life support. If they want to keep them alive and make a late-season push for the last Wild Card spot, they need a few players to lock in.

3 Players Who Need to Lock In to Keep Pirates' Playoff Hopes Alive

Jared Jones was one of the many Pirates players who went into a massive slump in August . Going into the month, he owned a quality 3.81 ERA, 3.43 FIP, and 1.02 WHIP over his first 11 starts and 52 innings coming off the injured list. In that time, he struck out 27.9% of batters, with just a 7.2% walk rate. Opposing hitters also batted below the Mendoza Line against him at .197.

Then, in five starts during August, Jones allowed 17 earned runs over just 20 2/3 innings of work. His K% fell to 24%, and his walk rate rose to 11.5%. Sure, a .383 batting average on balls in play didn't do him any favors, but opponents owned a 91.3 MPH exit velocity, 9.2% barrel rate, and 2.18 HR/9 ratio against him.

If his first start of September says anything, Jones is starting to lock back in again . He pitched six scoreless frames against the Los Angeles Angels. He allowed just three hits, with nine strikeouts, and just one walk allowed. While it was against a team with a combined OPS of .677, it is a step in the right direction for Jones. Returning to his July form, where he had a 2.00 ERA, 33.7% K%, and 6.1% BB%, would give the Pirates' rotation a much-needed boost of energy, giving them just enough to be playoff-ready.

Bryan Reynolds was a deserving All-Star . At the end of July, the veteran switch-hitter was slashing .268/.381/.453 with a .365 wOBA and 129 wRC+. Although Reynolds struck out at a 24% rate through his first 483 plate appearances, he also walked at a healthy 13.9% rate and had an above-average .189 isolated slugging percentage.

August did not go in Reynolds' favor. It was only 118 plate appearances, but he hit just .238/.322/.295 with a .285 wOBA and 74 wRC+. Reynolds still struck out at a similar 23.7% rate, but his walk rate fell to 10.2%, and he didn't hit a single home run during the month. A .323 xwOBA suggested some bad luck played a role, but it was not a month for Reynolds to be proud of overall.

Reynolds is looking like he is finding his groove again. Over his last 10 games at the time of this writing, he has 15 hits, including a home run, five walks, and only seven strikeouts over 45 plate appearances. His exit velocity in this stretch is over 94 MPH, and his xwOBA is over .400. It's a small sample size, but hitting the ball consistently hard, while drawing walks, and avoiding strikeouts at an above-average rate is a good sign. The Pirates will need him to figure it out down the stretch to keep their playoff hopes alive. Plus, it would be nice to get the Pirates' longest-tenured player into the playoffs for once.

Esmerlyn Valdez put on a historic show of power throughout his first few months of the major leagues. By the end of July, he was hitting .271/.366/.650, with a whopping 14 home runs and a .379 isolated slugging percentage over 164 plate appearances. While the young outfielder struck out over a third of the time (33.8%), he also drew a walk at a 12.8% pace. On top of that, Valdez was a shockingly good defender in the outfield.

However, like many Pirates players, Valdez did not have a memorable August, slashing .195/.337/.325 with an 88 wRC+. Opponents did not like pitching to him, as his free-pass percentage came in at 17.9%. However, his already high K% rose to 42.1%. He also only hit two home runs over 95 plate appearances in August.

Valdez has been one of the most pitched-around batters since the All-Star break. His 34.3% out-of-zone pitch rate is the highest among batters who have seen at least 1,000 pitches since the break. However, the lack of seeing any good strikes has seemingly thrown off his timing. Valdez isn't doing anything uncommon for a 22-year-old rookie, but for the Pirates' playoff hopes to stay alive, they need him to find something akin to his hot start in the late stages of the regular season.

articles.title: Five key takeaways from Florida's season-opening win over FAU Owls
articles.summary: Florida football defeats Florida Atlantic University in Jon Sumrall's first game as head coach of the Florida Gators. Here are five key takeaways.
articles.body:
Florida football opened the 2026 season with a convincing victory over FAU on Saturday night, but the Gators left the matchup with plenty to evaluate heading into the depth of their schedule.

The offense provided several reasons for optimism, particularly with the play of quarterback Aaron Philo, running back Jadan Baugh and a receiving corps that lived up to its preseason expectations.

At the same time, Florida's defense left much to be desired after allowing 21 points to an FAU offense that the Gators should have been able to contain more effectively.

Here are the biggest takeaways from Florida's season-opening 66-21 victory.

PHOTOS: Highlights from Florida's season-opening win vs FAU Owls

Aaron Philo looked solid in his Florida debut

If there were questions about whether Aaron Philo could handle the pressure of being Florida's starting quarterback, he provided plenty of answers Saturday night.

Philo completed 16 of 21 passes for 275 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in his first start for the Gators. More importantly, he consistently showed the poise and cerebral playmaking ability Florida will need from its quarterback as the competition gets tougher.

The transfer quarterback repeatedly used his legs to extend plays and keep the offense moving, eventually finding the end zone on the ground as well. There will obviously be much tougher tests ahead in SEC play, but Philo's debut provided an encouraging look.

Jadan Baugh entered the season with significant expectations, and he wasted little time showing why.

The All-SEC back exploded for 160 rushing yards and three touchdowns against FAU, giving Florida some of its most effortless touchdowns. Baugh was already in the conversation, but tonight's production puts him squarely in the conversation for the Doak Walker Award, which is presented annually to the nation's top running back.

And if he continues producing at this level against SEC competition, the conversation could eventually become much bigger.

Vernell Brown III, receiving corps are formidable weapons

The early returns on the receiving corps are encouraging. Vernell Brown III was particularly impressive, surpassing 100 receiving yards while providing Philo with a reliable yards-after-catch option throughout the night.

If Brown and the rest of the receiving corps continue to perform at a consistent level, Florida could have one of the more dangerous passing attacks in the SEC.

Florida's defense left something to be desired

For as encouraging as the offensive performance was, Florida's defense was arguably the biggest disappointment of the night.

The Gators allowed FAU to score 21 points, a number that should raise some questions considering the expectations surrounding Florida's defense heading into the season.

The program will need to clean up some of the issues that allowed the Owls to find success offensively, particularly before the Gators begin facing the more talented offenses on their schedule.

A 21-point performance isn't enough to erase the positives from a season-opening victory, but it does serve as an early warning and something to look out for as SEC play looms.

Florida's overall performance gives Gator Nation reason to be optimistic

Florida got the result it needed to begin the 2026 season, and the offense provided plenty of reasons for optimism.

Philo looked comfortable in his first start; Baugh immediately established himself as one of the nation's most dangerous running backs and players. The defense, however, remains the biggest question mark.

The Gators won't be able to rely on simply outscoring opponents once SEC play arrives. Saturday's victory was a strong first step in the Sumrall era.

articles.title: Zverev and Gauff ease into US Open last 16 but Alex Eala falls to Jovic
articles.summary: Filipina Alex Eala lost a three-set thriller to American Iva Jovic, as Naomi Osaka overcame Elise Mertens to progress.
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev kept his bid for a second Grand Slam title alive with a straightforward win over Alejandro Tabilo, while Coco Gauff stayed strong to reach the fourth round of the US Open as several of her fellow Americans crashed out.

Naomi Osaka overcame a mental and physical battle to outlast Belgium’s Elise Mertens in a three-setter on Louis Armstrong Stadium on Saturday.

Two of the brightest young prospects in the women’s draw, and close friends off the court, put on a show as American Iva Jovic edged Filipina Alexandra Eala in a thrilling clash at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

After back-to-back five-setters, top seed Zverev finally enjoyed a quieter night as he overcame a small mid-match dip to see off Chile’s Tabilo 6-2, 7-6(2), 6-2.

“I think today was definitely much better than the last couple of days. I think I improved a lot from the baseline,” Zverev said.

“I wasn’t happy with the second set. I think, especially at the end of the second set, I lost focus a little bit. I was not moving as well. I was not playing as well. But I think the first and third sets are a big improvement to the other days. I’ll try to focus on that.”

Japanese 13th seed Osaka, a two-time US Open champion, worked through a challenge after letting slip a one-set and break advantage before managing an Achilles niggle to beat Mertens 6-3, 3-6, 7-5.

The match was as much a test of Osaka’s composure as her tennis, with the 28-year-old showing visible frustration before regaining control in the decider.

“Honestly, I didn’t feel like I played amazing, and it was really getting me down, like I was very negative on myself, so I’m really sorry about my behaviour,” an emotional Osaka said.

Jovic, 18, and Eala, 21, traded momentum throughout a contest that lasted more than three hours before the American prevailed 7-5, 3-6, 7-5. Jovic, the 14th seed, will next face compatriot and fan favourite Gauff.

Fourth seed Gauff had earlier provided the day’s clearest positive for the home fans, the 22-year-old beating Spain’s Cristina Bucsa 6-3, 6-4, as the 2023 champion looks to win a third Grand Slam crown.

Second seed Elena Rybakina continued her quest for a third major title and the top spot in the WTA rankings, advancing after a 7-6(6), 6-3 win over Yuliia Starodubtseva.

Australian Open champion Rybakina avenged the second-round defeat she suffered to the Ukrainian at the French Open. The Kazakh will face Osaka for a place in the quarterfinals.

Iga Swiatek, the 2022 champion, beat Marie Bouzkova 7-6(3), 7-6(3), while French Open champion Mirra Andreeva advanced by downing Nikola Bartunkova 6-2, 7-6(5).

The day had begun with a string of painful exits for the home players.

Past US Open finalists Taylor Fritz, Madison Keys and Amanda Anisimova crashed out in the third round, dealing a stinging blow to the home fans at Flushing Meadows.

Ninth seed Fritz had yet to drop a set in New York and looked on his way to another routine victory before Argentinian Francisco Cerundolo flipped the script and won 3-6, 4-6, 6-3, 6-4, 6-4.

It was the earliest exit in four years for the 2024 runner-up, and Cerundolo will next face Belgium’s Alexander Blockx, who shocked fifth seed Flavio Cobolli 6-7(4), 6-3, 6-0, 6-3.

The American women fared no better, as China’s Zheng Qinwen came back from a 5-0 deficit in the decider to beat 2017 runner-up Keys 1-6 7-6(3) 7-5 on the Grandstand, collapsing on the court in utter joy as she fought back from a career slump.

The Olympic champion reached the quarterfinals for the second straight time only two years ago but was forced to go through qualifying this time after a chronic right elbow injury derailed her career progress.

Last year’s runner-up and 10th seed Anisimova was unable to reverse her fortunes in a frustrating year at the majors, with a 6-2, 7-5 defeat by Anastasia Potapova.

Young American wildcard Michael Zheng was another casualty, unable to complete a comeback against Frenchman Arthur Gea in a 7-6(7), 3-6, 4-6, 6-3, 6-2 defeat. Gea became just the second lucky loser to reach the fourth round, after fellow countryman Corentin Moutet in 2022.

The day ended on a positive note for the home crowd, who spurred Learner Tien to a gritty 6-3, 1-6, 6-7(2), 6-3, 6-4 win over Czech Jakub Mensik.

articles.title: La tortura china del Freelander 8: lo despeñan montaña abajo y pretenden que siga funcionando
articles.standfirst: La nueva marca china de Chery ha sometido a su Freelander 8 a una prueba muy bestia...
articles.summary: La marca china de Chery ha sometido a su Freelander 8 a una prueba muy bestia...
articles.body: Los fabricantes chinos tienen una particular forma de probar la resistencia de sus modelos, como acabamos de ver en un vídeo publicado por Freelander, la marca asitática de Chery con el nombre del antiguo todoterreno de Land Rover que asusta solo de verlo. Se conoce como el Rollover Test y, básicamente, consiste en despeñar montaña abajo una unidad (al más puro estilo Top Gear) y comprobar si después de dar varias vueltas de campana, sus elementos clave siguen intactos. Hasta el punto de que el 'aprobado' final dependa de si el coche es capaz de arrancar... y seguir rodando. Y parece que el Freelander 8 no se iba a librar de su particular tortura china. Lo subieron a la cima de una especie de duna y, mediante una plataforma, lo lanzaron laterlamente montaña abajo para forzar el vuelco. A partir de ahí, la suerte está echada porque sólo dejará de dar vueltas de campana cuando la fuerza de la gravedad lo estime oportuno... Después de seis segundos eternos y cinco 'croquetas', el Freelander se detiene (sobre las ruedas) con daños evidentes en la carrocería y el interior 'patas arriba' por el despliegue de todos los airbag. Es entonces cuando los técnicos de Freelander pasan a comprobar los efectos del durísimo test de durabilidad revisando, sobre todo, los elementos estructurales del chasis, las puertas (que abren y cierran después de los golpazos, incluso funciona el sistema de cierre asistido), el techo, el estado de la batería... Pero lo más sorprendente es que después de los violentos impactos sufridos en la caída libre el Freelander 8 era capaz de reemprender la marcha, y no solo eso, sino que incluso circulaba sin problemas fuera de carretara, e incluso subiendo la ladera por la que habia sido lanzado sin contemplaciones. Por supuesto, la marca ha quedado tan orgullosa por el resultado que lo ha mostrado al mundo... y no ha dudado en conservar la unidad 'torturada' para mostrarla como prueba de la dureza de su Freelander 8, un modelo que ya está a al venta en China y que ha conseguido bastantes adeptos, ya que se han registrado hasta 10.000 pedidos en las primeras 48 horas de comercialización.

articles.title: Bayern's Neuer: Boos in Schalke homecoming 'are compliments'
articles.summary: Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer wasn't bothered by the boos and whistles in his homecoming to Gelsenkirchen for his likely last match at Schalke. "Thos...
articles.body:
Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer wasn't bothered by the boos and whistles in his homecoming to Gelsenkirchen for his likely last match at Schalke.

"Those are actually compliments, that's love. Every boo every time I touched the ball was a compliment," Neuer said after the goalless draw on Saturday evening.

Neuer has played for only two clubs in his career and even 15 years after his transfer to Bayern, he still has a special connection with his hometown club.

"I played here for over 20 years, so it was still a very emotional day for me-something truly special. Still, I would have liked to take the three points home with me," he said.

Schalke are making their long-awaited return to the Bundesliga after three years in the second division. Neuer, meanwhile, is likely playing the last season in his professional career.

The promoted side took an unexpected point against the German record champions and while Neuer had little to do in the evening, Schalke counterpart Loris Karius took centre stage with big saves.

"He's the right choice for Player of the Match. He stopped the three big chances we had. That was the key today," the Bayern number one said.

Schalke coach Miron Muslic recognized that "in the end, it was certainly a lucky point, but we gave it our all for Schalke, and that's what makes us strong."

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton unhappy with Ferrari execution in Monza F1 qualifying
articles.summary: Hamilton felt the Scuderia could have done better after ending up fifth in qualifying on its home turf
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton has somewhat implicitly expressed dissatisfaction with Ferrari 's execution in qualifying at Formula 1's Italian Grand Prix.

Hamilton was eighth-fastest in Q1, made it out of Q2 by just 0.001s, and ended up fifth in Q3, which he was disappointed with despite being just 0.225s down on polesetter Pierre Gasly .

Ferrari's qualifying rota meant Hamilton could choose whether to go out ahead of team-mate Charles Leclerc or behind him this weekend; the seven-time world champion logically opted to go second in order to benefit from the Monegasque's tow in the 'Temple of Speed'.

However, Hamilton failed to get that slipstream on his first Q3 run due to his tyres being prepared tardily, and he still was slower than the sister car on his second attempt – by 0.007s.

Asked about the cooperation between team-mates being important in Monza, the Briton pondered the question for a few seconds before deflectively replying: "What I can say is, Pierre did a great job. Clearly, looking from a distance, it looked like they worked really well as a team."

He went on to add: "The team was solely focused on trying to get an equal tow for each driver. And, as I said, we just stumbled."

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari

The Ferraris will eventually lock out the second row for the race, courtesy of Oscar Piastri 's three-place grid penalty for impeding Liam Lawson , though Hamilton is aware he's not the favourite for victory.

"That puts us in fighting chance, hopefully, with George [Russell]. That's one Mercedes up front, so hopefully that gives us a chance," he said.

"George has the fastest car, that's clear. Particularly if you see his Mercedes. We're lacking on straights still, and that's just the way it is."

And as the F1 season goes on, Hamilton grows more uncertain as to his title chances, with his deficit to Antonelli currently 59 points.

"There's light at the end of the tunnel, but it's getting dimmer the further we get through," he deplored. "And even though the team's doing an amazing job in bringing upgrades and pushing us forward – I'm so proud of everyone, I say it all the time, but it's because I really am – also at the track, we need to come correct and act accordingly to make sure we get the result we need."

articles.title: Notts lose Verreynne to South Africa for final games
articles.summary: Nottinghamshire lose wicketkeeper Kyle Verreynne for their last three Championship matches, following his call-up by South Africa.
articles.body:
County champions Nottinghamshire have been dealt a blow by losing wicketkeeper Kyle Verreynne for their last three games, following his call-up by South Africa.

Along with several other South Africans currently playing in England, the 29-year-old has been recalled home for the forthcoming visit of Australia.

The three-match Test series with the Aussies does not begin until 9 October, 12 days after the County Championship season finishes - but there are also three one-day internationals prior to that.

Verreynne had signed to play all of Nottinghamshire's Championship matches this summer - but the terms of his central contract with his home governing body take precedence.

Notts, who sit in second place, four points behind leaders Somerset and a point ahead of third-placed Warwickshire, will miss the matches against Hampshire, Sussex, and Yorkshire.

"It's not ideal that we're losing Kyle at this point in the season," said Nottinghamshire director of cricket Mick Newell.

"But we understand the decision made by Cricket South Africa.

"We've been very happy to have Kyle with us for most of the summer, during which his contributions have put us in a strong position as we head towards the final few matches.

"We hope to confirm a replacement for Kyle as soon as we're able to."

articles.title: How Bryson DeChambeau once suggested golf should solve slow play in the professional game
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau once called on the governing bodies to factor in how quickly players walk to their golf ball when assessing slow play, as he insisted that...
articles.body:
Bryson DeChambeau once called on the governing bodies to factor in how quickly players walk to their golf ball when assessing slow play, as he insisted that the criticism he gets is not fair.

DeChambeau has divided opinion throughout his career. His distinctive name and unique style put him on the radar of most golf fans while he was still an amateur.

Unfortunately, he has not always managed to make headlines for the right reasons.

Bryson DeChambeau defended himself over slow play criticism back in 2019

One of the controversies DeChambeau has sparked during his career concerns how long he can take over his shots.

The two-time US Open champion appears to be the most methodical player at the highest levels of the game, with DeChambeau making all sorts of calculations before he hits what appears to be a fairly straightforward shot.

It has to be said that DeChambeau seems to have got better at hitting the ball quicker in recent years. However, his pace of play has led to plenty of ridicule in the past.

Interestingly, and perhaps unsurprisingly, DeChambeau felt that the perception was unfair.

Speaking to the New York Post in 2019, the American claimed that his pace would be viewed very differently if the time he took to walk to the ball was taken into account.

He said: "How long does it take to walk from shot to shot or to a drive 320 yards out?"

"That takes about two and a half minutes compared to 40 seconds over a shot. We've got more of a potential to decrease the time it takes to play a round by walking a little bit faster. When you're talking about pace of play, you have to include the time it takes to walk.

"I can take 10 seconds longer to hit a shot, but if I walk 10 seconds faster the total aggregate time is the same, yet they're penalising me because I took 10 seconds longer over the ball. It doesn't make sense.

"For some people to say, 'I just go up there and hit it,' well that's good for you. If it works for you, it works for you. But I want to be as precise as possible heading into that shot. I want to be right on point and that just requires me to be a little faster walker."

How Bryson DeChambeau's slow play led to one of the game's most interesting rivalries

It was frustrations with DeChambeau's pace of play that sparked one of the game's most interesting rivalries of the last few decades.

Admittedly, it would have shocked few once it became apparent that Bryson DeChambeau was not universally liked on the PGA Tour before his departure for LIV Golf .

But it was Brooks Koepka who could not bite his tongue any longer. Koepka insisted back in 2019 that he could not understand how a longer hitter could need 75 seconds to do all of the calculations and hit a shot.

While he did not name DeChambeau, it seemed fairly clear who he was referring to.

There was a clash between DeChambeau and Koepka's caddie shortly after at that year's Northern Trust Open. And from there, the two players would go on to make no secret of the animosity between themselves.

In truth, Koepka probably would have found a reason to publicly hit out at DeChambeau at some stage anyway.

It seems Koepka was obviously in no mood to consider just how quickly DeChambeau walked to his golf ball.

articles.title: "It's Over": Clemson HC Breaks Silence After Lane Kiffin Gives Him Biggest Embarrassment Of His Career
articles.summary: Dabo Swinney had seen just about everything during his remarkable run at Clemson. National championships.
articles.body:
Dabo Swinney had seen just about everything during his remarkable run at Clemson. National championships. Playoff heartbreaks. Rivalry wins. Crushing losses. Nothing quite prepared him for Saturday night in Baton Rouge, as Lane Kiffin's LSU debut turned into a nightmare for the Clemson HC.

The Tigers dismantled Clemson 51-10 at Tiger Stadium. The 41-point loss was the worst defeat of Swinney's coaching career and Clemson's worst loss since a 54-7 defeat at Florida State in 2000.

For Dabo Swinney, the frustration was obvious. There was no long explanation. No attempt to soften what had just happened. "The best thing about that one is that it's over," the Tigers HC said after the game . That pretty much summed up Clemson's night.

Clemson had fewer than 100 yards of total offense for most of the night before a late touchdown drive padded the final numbers. The problems went far beyond the offense.

LSU piled up 644 total yards, including 309 on the ground, while Clemson managed just 145 yards all night. The Tigers also dominated the first-down battle 38-8, a stunning gap that showed just how thoroughly LSU controlled the game from start to finish.

LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt made the Clemson defense look overwhelmed from the opening quarter. He finished with 230 passing yards and a touchdown through the air while adding 113 rushing yards and two more scores. Dillin Jones also ran for 113 yards and two touchdowns as Kiffin's offense kept Clemson on its heels all night.

LSU converted 11 of 16 third-down opportunities and also converted its only fourth-down attempt. Clemson, meanwhile, managed just one conversion on 13 third-down tries. By the fourth quarter, Clemson's sideline looked defeated, and the stadium had begun to empty. Even Kiffin appeared surprised by just how badly Clemson unraveled.

"I didn't expect their offense to be that dysfunctional," Kiffin said after the game. "Our scout team scored more than they did against us."

It was not simply an opening-week defeat against a talented SEC opponent. It was a brutal mismatch between two programs that appeared to be moving in opposite directions.

LSU looked fast, aggressive, and confident, while Clemson looked stuck. By the third quarter, the Tigers had pushed the lead to 44-3. Clemson eventually found the end zone late, but by then the outcome had been decided.

Clemson's struggles in season openers have now become impossible to ignore. The Tigers have lost each of their last four, falling to Duke in 2023, Georgia in 2024, LSU in 2025, and now LSU again in 2026. The latest defeat was by far the most damaging, with Clemson getting overwhelmed 51-10 in Baton Rouge.

Dabo Swinney remained optimistic afterward, insisting Clemson is better than what it showed against LSU. "We've got a long way to go," he said. "We're going to get better." Next comes Georgia Southern. After what happened in Baton Rouge, Clemson needs that improvement to start immediately.

articles.title: Phillies 24-Year-Old Pitcher Faces ‘Enormous Financial Burden’ After Cancer Diagnosis
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies received an emotional update on a player who was hit with a brutal medical update while expecting his first child.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies have spent the past several years adding young pitching depth from across the baseball world, often taking chances on arms who still have room to develop. One of those pitchers joined the organization in 2024 after already making his way through multiple professional systems.

Gabriel Barbosa was originally signed by the Colorado Rockies as an international free agent in 2018 before moving through the Rockies and New York Yankees organizations. The Phillies selected the right-hander from the Yankees in the minor league phase of the 2024 Rule 5 Draft, giving him another opportunity to continue his professional career.

Barbosa, who is 24 years old, has continued working his way through the Phillies' minor league system, reaching Double-A and eventually making his Triple-A debut earlier this summer. But his baseball career has now been interrupted by a far more serious challenge, as he and his young family confront a cancer diagnosis and the financial strain that comes with it.

Philadelphia Phillies' Young Pitcher Faces Cancer Battle While Expecting First Child

Barbosa revealed his diagnosis publicly in an emotional Instagram post in July, explaining how quickly the news forced him to reconsider what mattered most.

"I was diagnosed with colon cancer," Barbosa wrote in an Instagram post . "I never imagined that at 24 years old I would be living something like this. In just a few minutes, I thought about everything: my health, my wife, our son on the way, my mother, my father, my sister, my entire family, my friends, my teammates and all the dreams I still want to achieve."

According to a GoFundMe organized by Rolando Fernandez and published on August 31, Barbosa was diagnosed with Stage 3 colon cancer after becoming ill while pitching at the Double-A level for the Phillies. He is undergoing immunotherapy and is scheduled for surgery in September, the same month that he and his wife, Pamela, are expecting their first child.

The timing makes an already difficult situation even more challenging for the young family. Barbosa's professional baseball journey had taken him from Brazil through the Rockies, Yankees and Phillies, while he also represented Brazil internationally.

MLB Scout Flags Financial Burden Facing Philadelphia Phillies' Pitcher After Cancer Diagnosis

The GoFundMe campaign is seeking financial assistance as Barbosa undergoes treatment while preparing to become a father.

"I'm creating this GoFundMe to help Gabriel and Pamela with the enormous financial burden associated with his cancer treatment, immunotherapy, surgery, medical expenses, and the challenges their young family will face in the months ahead," Fernandez wrote on the fundraiser's webpage . "No 24-year-old should have to choose between fighting for his health, preparing for the birth of his first child, and worrying about how to pay for it all."

As of this writing, the effort had raised more than $36,000 with a goal of $50,000.

articles.title: Verstappen Sounds the Alarm on Red Bull’s Monza Problems: “We Are Not Operating at 100%”
articles.summary: Max Verstappen will line up on the third row for the 2026 Italian Grand Prix, but the reigning world champion’s patience is wearing paper-thin. After qualify...
articles.body:
Max Verstappen will line up on the third row for the 2026 Italian Grand Prix , but the reigning world champion's patience is wearing paper-thin. After qualifying sixth with a 1:22.070—later promoted to fifth courtesy of Kimi Antonelli's power unit penalty—Verstappen laid bare an escalating laundry list of mechanical glitches that hijacked his RB22 right when it mattered most.

From sudden engine dropouts in traffic to a suspected rear axle failure and a chassis that refused to absorb Monza's unforgiving kerbs, Verstappen gave an unfiltered critique of Red Bull's recurring technical headaches.

Red Bull spent Friday night overhauling the car's setup, and for a brief window during final practice, the Dutchman looked poised to fight at the sharp end. But as soon as the pressure spiked in Q3, the car unraveled.

"I mean, I just want to have a car that is in a 100% state," Verstappen told the media bluntly when asked about his Sunday prospects. "That would be nice because we have too many weekends where things just, yeah, go wrong. You know, just stop, either brakes or, you know, we're not operating at 100%."

Verstappen acknowledged the engineering staff's overnight turnaround before lamenting how quickly it dissolved. "I was very happy with FP3. I think the team did a great job in terms of finding a much better balance in the car finally, but then yeah, we couldn't then translate that to qualifying."

A Suspected Rear Axle Failure for Red Bull

The most alarming development occurred under the rear bodywork. Verstappen reported that without making significant setup alterations between sessions, the handling abruptly altered between FP3 and qualifying.

"FP3 actually, we had a very good improvement overnight. The car was in a much better window, but then yeah, we didn't really touch the car too much going into qualifying and suddenly, yeah, I have a feeling that something failed on the rear axle again," Verstappen revealed. "Not the wing, but something else mechanically where we have to look into again. But it's not the first time this happens, but it happens at random times in the weekend. Unfortunately, now it happened to the most important part."

The mechanical gremlin immediately destroyed the RB22's compliance. While rivals rode Monza's high-speed chicanes with authority, Verstappen was left fighting a skittish machine.

"When you have these kinds of problems, it becomes super difficult to drive," he told the media. "The car is not complying anymore when it should do on bumps and kerbs. And that's just costing us time, unfortunately, because I actually thought that with how the car was responding in FP3, I didn't think I was fighting for pole, but it was quite a comfortable car to drive for once, and that was actually really nice. But unfortunately, then, yeah, we picked up another problem in qualifying."

Compounding the rear suspension issues, Verstappen found himself completely isolated in Q3. A planned tow from teammate Liam Lawson evaporated when the Kiwi was impeded in Turn 2 during Q2 and failed to advance.

Left to scramble for track position against the Mercedes duo of Antonelli and George Russell, Verstappen suffered yet another powertrain scare.

"I was trying to accelerate, and then the engine cut out," Verstappen said, detailing the messy out-lap sequence. "I had so many things going on. It's super complicated." When questioned by reporters on whether the car's sluggish low-speed behavior came down to driver inputs or setup, Verstappen shut down the premise: "Well, from what I just explained, not very good."

Despite the frustration boiling over, Verstappen went out of his way to defend Red Bull's trackside mechanics, pointing the finger directly at persistent design and component vulnerabilities that have trailed the team across multiple development cycles.

"No, I think the mechanics are very good," Verstappen told the media when asked if garage errors were creeping in. "It's just some components on the car, I think we are not fully on top of them."

Asked if the aggressive pursuit of weight reduction had compromised structural reliability, Verstappen dismissed the theory, revealing that the team's technical gremlins aren't even exclusive to the 2026 platform.

"No, no, because I've had these problems also on the old car."

With Pierre Gasly starting on a shock pole and the Mercedes-Ferrari contingent packing out the top rows, Verstappen faces a grueling 53-lap fight down the Temple of Speed—not just against his championship rivals, but against the stubborn hardware under his own right foot.

articles.body:
Manchester United's failure to strengthen the left-back position this summer remains a concern. The Red Devils were linked with several candidates for the position, including Newcastle United's Lewis Hall , but ended the transfer window without reinforcing the area.

INEOS' focus was on the midfield, which had been weakened by the departure of Casemiro at the end of last season. United invested over £150 million in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, and Carlos Baleba to address the situation.

That left them with limited funds to secure a deal for a new left-back or a striker. The Red Devils are now relying on Luke Shaw to maintain the high standards he set last season, during which he started every Premier League game.

However, the Englishman has entered the final year of his contract at Old Trafford and he is yet to sign a new deal. Shaw was injury-free last season, but has a history of fitness-related issues.

United have to prepare for a fixture-congested season

United's need for a new left-back has been heightened by their involvement in the Champions League this season. The Red Devils qualified for the premier European club competition after finishing third in the Premier League last campaign.

There is a belief that Shaw could struggle to play three games a week, given that Michael Carrick's team will also be aiming for an extended run in the FA Cup and the EFL Cup. While the transfer window is closed, there remains an opportunity to sign free agents.

Among them is David Alaba, who is highly experienced and has won several trophies, including four Champions League titles. The Austrian is well acquainted with the demands of playing for elite clubs, having represented Bayern Munich and Real Madrid in his career.

A previous report relayed by The Peoples Person named the 34 year old as a possible option for United this year. Journalist Tyrone Marshall has now shed light on the club's stance on the matter.

In a Q&A with United fans for the Manchester Evening News , Marshall was asked why United are not considering a move for free agents like Sergio Ramos, Dani Carvajal and Alaba. He responded: "From what I have been told, United aren't looking at the free agent market."

"Many of these players available are past their best, Ramos and Carvajal certainly fit that description. Others have been released because their games have regressed, such as Alaba."

"Essentially, they are free agents for a reason, but they are also players who in the past have been paid very handsomely. They don't fit the recruitment model that Ineos have introduced at Old Trafford."

"The only possible way this changes is if Luke Shaw picks up a significant injury and United are left with no left-back at all, but even then it's far from guaranteed."

While Alaba is immensely experienced, he struggled to stay fit during the final years of his spell at the Santiago Bernabeu. As such, a move for the veteran defender may represent an unnecessary risk.

articles.title: Fall sports are here. See how likely that sport is to take a kid to college
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of student athletes are returning to their college teams this fall. Earning a spot on collegiate rosters, or athletic scholarships, takes years of work from young athletes — and thousands of dollars from their parents in fees, travel and other costs.
articles.body: Hundreds of thousands of student athletes are returning to their college teams this fall. Earning a spot on collegiate rosters, or athletic scholarships, takes years of work from young athletes — and thousands of dollars from their parents in fees, travel and other costs. But the odds are long to get them there: Just 7% of high school athletes will compete on a college roster at any level, while 2% will go on to earn a National College Athletic Association, or NCAA, athletic scholarship. An even smaller fraction will go pro. So as parents are ordering fall uniforms and planning tournament entries, CNN analyzed the odds for a high schooler to make a college roster, based on data compiled by Patrick O’Rourke on the website ScholarshipStats.com. A more popular sport doesn’t mean longer odds, since more schools sponsor collegiate teams. Football was by far the most popular high school sport, with more than 1 million high school athletes competing in the 2022-2023 school year, and more than 96,000 going on to play in college. Nearly one-third of those athletes played at the Division I level, typically schools with the more elite and well-funded sports programs. The size of football rosters — with most teams exceeding 100 players — helped those athletes’ odds further: 11:1 to make any college roster and 33:1 to make a Division I team. Track and field was the second most common high school boys’ sport that year, with more than 580,000 high school track and field athletes vying for spots on just over 1,200 college teams. Those boys’ 16:1 odds of making any college roster were slightly longer than they were for the more than 465,000 girls competing to make one of more than 1,300 collegiate teams. Their odds were 13:1. The more obscure sports had slimmer odds. Female wrestlers vying for a spot on one of the four Division I women’s teams in 2022-2023 faced the longest odds by far: 709:1. For male wrestlers, the odds were still slim but much less challenging: 86:1. Female bowlers had better odds than either at making a DI team: 79:1. The cost, and benefits, of youth sports There are caveats to these numbers: Just 70% of female high school athletes go on to play in college, while just about half of male high schoolers go on to play collegiately, according to O’Rourke’s data analysis. Recent policy changes have cleared the way for college athletes to earn money from competing at that level, through scholarships at NCAA Division I schools or payments for their name, image and likeness, or NIL. But NCAA teams don’t award scholarships to every eligible player, and NIL earnings are highly concentrated in major sports like basketball and football, O’Rourke’s analysis found when he crunched the numbers for his new site NIL-NCAA.com. “If it was me, instead of paying a gazillion dollars on youth sports, I’d put the money in a 529,” O’Rourke told CNN. “Because that’ll play for college no matter what.” Money isn’t the only reason athletes might pursue a spot on a college roster — athletic talent can give students an edge in admissions. While Ivy League schools, and other competitive academic institutions, have impossibly low general admission rates, many have student-athletes making up as much as a fifth of their whole student body — a possible opportunity for kids with athletic talents, O’Rourke said. Childhood sports are good for children’s physical, mental and emotional health and development. And of course, just darn good fun.

articles.title: Gators start season strong with blowout of FAU. We hand out the grades
articles.summary: Florida football dominated FAU in Jon Sumrall's debut as head coach at The Swamp. For the Owls, they entered the game as 26.5-point underdogs.
articles.body:
The Jon Sumrall era couldn't have gotten a much better start for the Florida Gators .

For FAU's second-year head coach Zach Kittley , his team were 26.5-point underdogs and are seeking their first winning season in six seasons.

With no shortage of strong performances, Florida football took care of business against Florida Atlantic with a 66-21 victory on Saturday, Sept. 5 in Gainesville.

The 66 points were the most points in the Gators have scored in a season opener since 1994.

UF's newly named starting quarterback Aaron Philo accounted for three of his four touchdowns by halftime, which helped take a 38-14 lead by the half.

In the first quarter, Philo connected with Vernell Brown III for a 49-yard touchdown and then later Bailey Stockton for a 12-yard touchdown. Kicker Patrick Durkin capped off the quarter with a career-long 53-yard field goal.

FAU got on the board at the start of the second quarter, but the Gators answered quickly as Philo scored easily on a 3-yard run to build a 24-7 lead.

The Owls managed to punch in another score with under seven minutes left in the half, but from there UF's star running back Jadan Baugh took over the game as he scored twice before the end of the half.

He then eclipsed the 100-yard mark within the first minute of the second half with a 61-yard run to set up his third touchdown of the game.

Brown finished the game with six catches for 117 yards. On defense, DJ Coleman and Dijon Johnson each came down with an interception.

Here's what happened in the Gators' win over the Owls.

Grading the Florida Gators' opening win against FAU

The Florida Gators weren't perfect, as Sumrall predicted, but were fairly crisp and efficient in racing to a 38-14 halftime lead. Florida scored 14 points off two first-half turnovers and scored five touchdowns and a field goal on its first six offensive possessions.

Overall, Florida ran up its most points since beating Samford 70-52 on November 13, 2021. It was also the highest for a Florida team in a season opener since UF beat New Mexico State 70-21 under Steve Spurrier to start the 1994 season.

Sumrall, hired from Tulane on November 30, 2025, is trying to establish physical and mental toughness in a UF program that's endured four losing seasons in its last five years.

Here's how UF graded out following its season opening win over the Owls.

Even with starting wide receiver Eric Singleton Jr. sidelined most of the game, Florida's offense put forth a dominant performance. Starting QB Aaron Philo went 16 of 21 for 275 yards with three TDs passing, one TD rushing and an interception that deflected off the hands of receiver Micah Mays Jr.

Philo was pulled late in the third quarter with Florida up 52-21. Preseason All-American running back Jadan Baugh had 14 carries for 160 yards and three TDs as Florida moved up and down the field at will. It was a near flawless debut for Florida football offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner other than a few high snaps by center Harrison Moore.

The good? Florida football's defense forced three takeaways on interceptions by safety DJ Coleman and cornerback Dijon Johnson and a fumble forced by Brendan Bett and recovered by Myles Johnson.

The bad? The Gators gave up a boatload of yards and had issues at times slowing down FAU's fast-paced passing attack. Florida didn't generate much of a pass rush as well but UF's secondary had a few coverage breakdowns that will need to be fixed moving forward.

Tulane transfer Patrick Durkin drilled a 53-yard field goal in his UF debut. Florida's punt and kick coverage teams kept FAU from springing any long returns. Backup kicker Liam Padron even got in late to kick the final extra point.

A fairly good debut for Sumrall as the Gators brought energy and offense back to The Swamp after the moribund Billy Napier era. Florida coaches will need to get to work on shoring up some issues on defense to prepare for the grind of SEC play.

articles.title: "A real wake-up call" – RB Leipzig boss responds after shock defeat to Werder Bremen
articles.summary: After RB Leipzig opened their Bundesliga campaign with a 3–0 win over Borussia Mönchengladbach, Martin Demichelis’ side were brought back down to earth with...
articles.body:
After RB Leipzig opened their Bundesliga campaign with a 3–0 win over Borussia Mönchengladbach, Martin Demichelis' side were brought back down to earth with a surprise 3–1 defeat to Werder Bremen on Saturday.

RB Leipzig managing director for sport Marcel Schäfer described the defeat as a "real wake-up call" ahead of the club's Champions League opener against Como on Thursday.

"It was a real wake-up call – perhaps at the right time as well. We've already got another important game on Thursday, so we can't afford to dwell on this for long. At the same time, given the standards we set ourselves, we can't simply brush this performance aside. We have to learn the right lessons from it and produce a response," Schäfer said in a post-match interview.

Leipzig were without key players such as Castello Lukeba and Brajan Gruda, but Schäfer refused to use their absences as an excuse.

"We fell well short in a lot of areas. The players we were missing are no excuse for that. We still had enough players on the pitch who have already shown what they can do at both club and international level. I therefore expected a very different performance," he said.

"We moved the ball too slowly and didn't get our wide players into the one-v-one situations where they can make a difference. We also didn't get enough bodies into the box. Having lots of possession, corners and crosses is all well and good, but what matters is what you make of them. We didn't find enough ways to break down a side defending very deep."

articles.title: ‘Need To Be Fired for Corruption and Cheating’ — Calls Mount For Big Ten Refs To Be Fired As Suspicion Hangs Over Michigan-WMU Thriller
articles.summary: Michigan narrowly avoided an upset against Western Michigan, escaping with a controversial 13-12 win. The Broncos appeared to have pulled off a stunning win...
articles.body:
Michigan narrowly avoided an upset against Western Michigan, escaping with a controversial 13-12 win.

The Broncos appeared to have pulled off a stunning win when Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood's first Hail Mary fell incomplete as the clock seemingly hit zero. However, the officials' ensuing decision gave the Wolverines another chance, dramatically changing the outcome and sparking reactions from college football fans.

Michigan's Win Over WMU Sparks Furious Backlash Against Refs

Western Michigan players initially believed they had pulled off a major, major upset against Michigan and began celebrating, but officials cut those celebrations short by initiating a replay review, which appeared to show the game clock hitting 0:00 before the ball made contact with a Broncos defender.

Officials determined that one second remained on the clock, giving Michigan one final opportunity. Underwood made the most of it, finding JJ Buchanan for the game-winning touchdown.

Western Michigan president Russ Kavalhuna called for the ending to be reviewed, while fans strongly criticized the officiating.

"Game between Michigan and Western Michigan was officiated by a Big Ten crew led by referee Jim Wharrie. Jim and crew need to be fired for corruption and cheating. There was NO time left on the clock," one fan remarked .

"Are these all the refs on the payroll?" wrote Bad Sports Refs , an account that claims to expose bad calls and referee missteps.

"Refs just robbed Western Michigan at gunpoint," Bad Sports Refs wrote in another tweet.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

Several hours after Michigan secured the narrow win, the Big Ten released a statement explaining why officials restored the second. The conference also provided the video replay that officials reviewed along with the audio of their discussion.

The alternate camera angle appeared to support the ruling, showing a Western Michigan defender touching the ball after stepping out of bounds with one second still showing on the stadium clock.

MAC commissioner Jon Steinbrecher later said he contacted the Big Ten to seek an explanation for the controversial ending. After receiving the conference's response, Steinbrecher indicated he was satisfied with the explanation.

However, that did little to stop the criticism, as fans continued to mock Michigan over the way it escaped with the victory.

"The refs in the Michigan game legitimately just cheated. Everyone of them should be fired," one said .

"One of the biggest crimes in sports history just happened to Western Michigan," veteran analyst Jason Whitlock wrote .

"Officials have to be held accountable. Stick those officials at the press conference and explain to America why there was a second left to screw WMU for Michigan to throw a Hail Mary. They'll be officiating next week. Zero repercussions for failing their job. Zero," analyst Garrett Armbrust ranted .

The controversy has overshadowed what Michigan hoped would be an impressive start to the Kyle Whittingham era.

The Wolverines entered the matchup as heavy favorites behind former five-star quarterback Underwood, but their performance hardly reflected the talent gap on paper as they struggled to put away Western Michigan.

articles.title: Haaland admits Arsenal have an advantage over Man City in title race
articles.summary: Erling Haaland believes Arsenal have an advantage over Manchester City as the two clubs begin what could develop into another battle at the top of the Premie...
articles.body:
Erling Haaland believes Arsenal have an advantage over Manchester City as the two clubs begin what could develop into another battle at the top of the Premier League.

City have made a perfect start to the new campaign, winning all three of their league matches, but Haaland believes Arsenal's greater continuity could work in their favour.

As reported by The Standard , Haaland believes the amount of time Mikel Arteta's players have spent together gives Arsenal an edge over a Manchester City side that is still evolving.

"Arsenal have played together for a long time and have built this up over a longer period, a bit like City had when I first joined," Haaland said.

"We're still in a kind of rebuilding phase, but the transfer window has been fantastic, I have to say."

The Norwegian was nevertheless full of praise for City's recruitment, saying the club had brought in both "fantastic footballers" and people who fit well into the squad.

It is an interesting admission from arguably Arsenal's biggest title rival.

Manchester City have hardly looked like a side struggling to rebuild, having taken maximum points from their opening three games. Haaland himself scored the only goal in Saturday's 1-0 victory over Coventry City.

Yet his comments highlight something that could prove important over the course of a long season.

Arteta has had time to develop this Arsenal side, and many of his key players know exactly what is expected of them and each other.

Haaland clearly sees value in that stability.

The challenge for Arsenal is turning that perceived advantage into results.

They face Chelsea at the Emirates on Sunday afternoon knowing victory would move them level with City at the top of the table.

It is still extremely early in the season, of course, but after City started with three straight victories, Arsenal will want to ensure they keep pace.

articles.body:
Last March's 3-0 win for Nottingham Forest at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium provided the platform for the visitors' survival bid while leaving Spurs floundering until the final day.

Since then Spurs have spent over £300m on new players - contributing to the record £3.49bn Premier League outlay this summer.

Sandro Tonali, Jon Paul Van Hecke, Savio and Omar Marmoush were the new signings who started on Saturday, with Roberto de Zerbi remaining calm after another blank.

"We bought very, very good players but you can't just build the team with the names like in Football Manager," he told Sky Sports.

"We are disappointed for the result but for the performance very happy. Considering we started to work together last Thursday for the first time, for the first day.

"We have to improve in every part of football, organisation with and without the ball. Even today I thought we defended very well.

"We have to work because I think we played very well with the ball, we found the solution. I think we can be much better in the final third."

A draw was Tottenham's eighth in the league this year, their most across a calendar year since 2020, and they failed to have a shot on target in a top-flight match for the first time since April 2022 against Brentford under Antonio Conte.

Spurs have had 38 shots in the league this season with an expected goals of 3.3 and former midfielder Danny Murphy agreed with De Zerbi over what the visitors lacked.

"When Spurs did get in really good areas, they just rushed it and shot when they maybe should've passed," he told BBC Sport.

"They made the wrong choice on pullbacks or crosses when they're getting in wide areas, taking men on one too many times when they've already got the space.

"They were just missing that little bit of calmness and composure that you expect from top quality players.

"It takes time for some players [to find chemistry]. You could argue that Marmoush and Savio know each other anyway and bright footballers quickly learn each other's runs and movements.

"From a midfielder to a forward perspective, you're not always sure what they're going to do. Whereas if you played with someone for a while, it comes more naturally. So those relationships will build."

articles.title: Vladimir Kramnik reacts to Levon Aronian’s 'modest confidence' after grandmaster says he is better than many
articles.summary: Chess News: Levon Aronian’s candid assessment of his chess career has drawn a pointed reaction from former world champion Vladimir Kramnik, after the American gra.
articles.body: Levon Aronian’s candid assessment of his chess career has drawn a pointed reaction from former world champion Vladimir Kramnik, after the American grandmaster said that reaching No. 2 in the world was already a “miracle” for him.In an exclusive interview with The Times of India, Aronian was asked whether he had any regrets about never becoming the classical World Champion. The 43-year-old was unequivocal: he said he had no regrets whatsoever, adding that he had never rated himself too highly as a chess player."The fact that I was No. 2 in the world is already a miracle''Levon Aronian spoke about whether he has any regrets about never becoming World Champion:"No, I have no regrets whatsoever. First of all, I never valued myself so highly as a chess player. Of course, I have talent, and of course I'm better than many World Champions in my understanding of chess. But the very fact that I reached No. 2 in the world rankings is already a miracle to me. Because my chess knowledge used to be much worse before.Generally, I'm not sure that setting up goals is a good thing for you. Sometimes it only adds anxiety, and there's already plenty of that in our world. It's better to simply enjoy yourself and appreciate what you have," Levon told TOI.The remarks soon caught the attention of Kramnik, who responded on X.Kramnik, the classical world champion from 2000 to 2007, described Aronian as a “remarkable and extraordinary chessplayer”, but appeared amused by the Armenian-born grandmaster's assessment of his own abilities.“I would call this claim ‘modest confidence’,” Kramnik wrote before questioning Aronian's assertion that he was better than many world champions in terms of chess understanding.“better than MANY world champions” in chess understanding? Hard to judge, but quite a statementKramnik's response adds an interesting layer to Aronian's comments. Rather than questioning Aronian's achievements, his post highlights just how extraordinary the grandmaster's career has been.Aronian came remarkably close to the summit of classical chess without ever winning the World Championship. He reached No. 2 in the FIDE rankings and a peak rating of 2830, while winning the World Cup twice, in 2005 and 2017. He also helped Armenia win three Chess Olympiad gold medals.His career also includes world titles in faster formats, making his absence from the list of classical world champions one of the more notable “what ifs” in modern chess.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
