articles.title: San Siro’s roar, El Toro’s instinct: Inter vs. Napoli in five moments
articles.summary: There are nights when the best moments are born of instinct. A feeling, an intuition that events might unfold a certain way, followed by the decision to trus...
articles.body:
There are nights when the best moments are born of instinct. A feeling, an intuition that events might unfold a certain way, followed by the decision to trust it and go with your gut. When Napoli scored their second goal, it might have been easy to lose faith, but neither the team nor San Siro wavered for a single second. The comeback was there for the taking.

Only three matchdays into the season, Inter vs. Napoli has already earned its place among the campaign's most memorable games, one that will live long in the memory: a sweltering evening, a red-hot San Siro, the return of Thu-La as both opened their accounts for the season and celebrated together on the barrier, and a comeback never before achieved against the Partenopei, completed with courage, heart and pride.

Let's relive the drama of Inter vs. Napoli through five defining moments from an extraordinary evening at San Siro.

The match began at a relentless pace, with chances coming thick and fast as Inter applied intense pressure for much of the first half. Chivu's side played high up the pitch and frequently regained possession in the opposition half, driven in large part by Yann Bisseck's constant forward surges. The German produced a performance, particularly before the break, in which he seemed to cover several areas of the pitch at once.

Bisseck repeatedly stepped in to win the ball, gave Napoli no room to breathe and pressed them deep inside their own half. In possession, he moved into an inside position, almost as a right-sided number ten, freeing up the flank for Diouf and providing an option between the lines for Barella.

He was everywhere defensively, too. When Hojlund broke clear and drove towards goal, Bisseck waited for the right moment before making a superb recovery tackle. At the other end, he nearly produced a number ten's finish of his own: after receiving the ball in the box, he nutmegged his marker and unleashed a powerful left-footed strike that flew narrowly wide. Yann was irrepressible, and San Siro could scarcely believe its eyes.

Rasmus Hojlund's left-footed strike found the bottom corner to Martinez's right (53'), just three minutes after Politano's opener. It was a brutal double blow after a first half packed with chances and played at relentless intensity. Inter now had a mountain to climb against a strong and determined Napoli side. Yet San Siro was alive. The scoreboard read Inter 0-2 Napoli, but the Nerazzurri faithful knew there was still a long way to go at the Meazza. If anything, the noise grew louder. All the team needed was a spark to ignite the flame.

The stadium roared, stirring itself and the players into life. The message was clear: 40 minutes is an eternity. We are with you, and we believe until the end. Inter fed off that energy and the adrenaline pouring down from the stands. What had seemed like the beginning of the end became the turning point: within three minutes, everything had changed.

As we said, it took Inter just three minutes to lay the foundations for the comeback. It was a fierce response, fuelled by a determination to show their strength, refuse to buckle under adversity and turn the match around at any cost. It was no coincidence that captain Lautaro was the man to pull one back. No player embodies Inter's spirit on the pitch and their desire to achieve the seemingly impossible more than he does.

This was when instinct began to suggest that the comeback really was on, with plenty of time left to complete it. The goal came down to split-second timing, anticipation and awareness. Zielinski crossed from the right towards the back post, where Dimarco timed his run perfectly and volleyed the ball back across goal with his left foot. Lautaro was waiting, anticipating the cross before anyone else and beating Rrahmani to the ball to finish into an empty net. Three touches were all it took to breach Napoli's wall. The captain grabbed the ball from the net, roused San Siro and led the charge. The game was alive again. Anything was possible.

While both teams were still in the dressing rooms at half-time, Marcus Thuram was already back out on the pitch without a bib, completing his warm-up before coming on. His expression was focused; he was determined to make an impact and celebrate at San Siro again. The last time he had done so was on 3 May, on Scudetto night.

He entered the action at the start of the second half and, within minutes, watched Napoli score twice. But when Lautaro immediately pulled one back, Marcus was fired up. Determined to help the team, he used his physical strength to do battle first with Marin and then with Badiashile, roaming across the entire front line and constantly looking for space. He sent a header crashing against the post but kept believing. His reward arrived in the 82nd minute, bringing back the feeling every striker lives for.

Carlos Augusto crossed from the left and Tikus timed his leap perfectly, rising above Badiashile and directing a header into the bottom corner to Meret's right. San Siro went wild, and Thuram unleashed a furious celebration. He raced towards the Curva with eyes wide, muscles tensed and teeth clenched, overcome with adrenaline. Then came his roar to the entire stadium: "Now let's go and win it!" Welcome back, Marcus.

Back to instinct, then. Once the score reached 2-2, all structure disappeared and every possible outcome was suddenly on the table. Thuram fired over from a promising position, and Neres did the same at the other end. Both teams were stretched, with every attack threatening to produce another chance.

San Siro held its breath when Anguissa met Lucca's volley from point-blank range but failed to find the unguarded net. It was a sign, a moment that stirred something in both the team and the Nerazzurri faithful. There was still all of stoppage time to find a winner, and the stadium was at boiling point. Barella's right-footed effort was tipped over by Meret, and from the resulting corner, one of the season's most memorable images began to take shape.

Jones crossed from the left towards the far post, where the ball remained loose between Bisseck and Akanji, Lucca and Di Lorenzo. The Swiss defender reacted quickest, nudging it on towards Lautaro Martinez. One almost imperceptible detail captured the instinct that made the difference: Lautaro's anticipation and goalscoring intuition were evident in the tiny adjustment steps he took before Akanji had even managed to divert the ball. The captain had already prepared for the possibility that it might fall his way, reading the situation before anyone else.

His instinct was rewarded. El Toro stretched out his left boot as he slid in, unleashing pandemonium as the sun set over San Siro. Lautaro climbed onto the barrier and roared with the Meazza; Chivu, Dimarco and the entire bench raced across, while Thuram joined him up high. It was glorious Nerazzurri chaos.

At the final whistle, the captain dropped to his knees, overcome with emotion and exhaustion, while Tikus raced across the pitch to find him and wrap him in an embrace. Inter had won a wild, wonderful and fiercely contested match, maintaining their perfect start to the season.

articles.title: Security forced to intervene as Percassi confronts D’Amico after Roma’s win over Atalanta
articles.summary: Multiple sources in Italy claim that Atalanta CEO Luca Percassi confronted and insulted Roma sporting director Tony D’Amico following the Giallorossi’s drama...
articles.body:
Multiple sources in Italy claim that Atalanta CEO Luca Percassi confronted and insulted Roma sporting director Tony D'Amico following the Giallorossi's dramatic win over La Dea on Saturday, forcing security staff to intervene.

There still seems to be bitter blood between Atalanta and their ex-sporting director D'Amico, who left La Dea to join Roma earlier this summer.

Luca Percassi Vice Chairman of Atalanta (Photo by Jonathan Moscrop/Getty Images)

According to several Italian sources, including Corriere dello Sport , which quoted 'direct witnesses', Atalanta CEO Percassi confronted D'Amico at full time and began insulting him, but the Roma director refused to respond.

Percassi reportedly followed D'Amico to the car park at the Stadio Olimpico, and the security staff was forced to intervene to restore calm.

According to Corriere dello Sport, friction between D'Amico and Percassi, who also serves as the Lega Serie A vice-president, dates back to two years ago, when Gian Piero Gasperini left Atalanta to join Roma.

Official: Tony D'Amico joins Roma as the club's new sporting director following four seasons with Atalanta (@ASRoma via X)

The Italian tactician was followed by D'Amico earlier this summer, upsetting Atalanta, who initially hadn't allowed the 46-year-old to move to the Stadio Olimpico despite having already secured an agreement with Cristiano Giuntoli as his replacement.

Corriere dello Sport and other sources say that Roma consider Percassi's behaviour unacceptable and will take all the necessary action to protect D'Amico, while Atalanta have not commented or reacted to the reports so far.

articles.title: Takeaways from Maryland football’s season-opening 62-0 rout of Hampton
articles.summary: A dominant rushing attack coupled with sound defense sealed the deal for the Terps.
articles.body:
Maryland football dismantled Hampton, 62-0, to start off its 2026 campaign, extending the nation's longest active nonconference win streak to 19 games

The Terps recorded 646 total yards — the program's most since 2020 — and backed it up with a dominant defensive display. After taking a 41-point lead in the third quarter, Maryland gave its depth pieces a chance to shine.

With the Big Ten's worst rush attack last season, head coach Michael Locksley made it a point of emphasis to relieve some stress off Malik Washington's shoulders — he ranked sixth nationally in pass attempts in 2025.

"For us to have any chance to be successful each week is going to start with our ability to run the football," head coach Michael Locksley said. "I thought today was a good start."

That came to fruition in Maryland's season opener.

DeJuan Williams broke loose on a 94-yard rushing touchdown on the Terps' second drive of the game — a sign of what was to come. Williams eclipsed 100 rushing yards nearly nine minutes into the game, something that only Washington managed to do in 2025.

While Williams shouldered the offensive load early on, he picked up a knock early in the second quarter. That allowed Iverson Howard and USC transfer Harry Dalton III to get more snaps, and they capitalized.

Howard was Maryland's lead back during the remaining three quarters, finishing with 12 carries for 66 rushing yards. He punched in a pair of short-yardage rushing touchdowns, marking his first career scores.

Despite being an undersized back, Dalton was explosive with his carries. He averaged 5.6 yards per attempt, with a nine-yard rushing touchdown capping off backup quarterback Cardell Williams' first drive as a Terp.

Washington and Williams got involved in the run game as well, combining for 53 of the team's 365 rushing yards.

Maryland had just nine rushing touchdowns throughout the entirety of the 2025 season. It had six on Saturday — the program's most since 2001. While Hampton allowed 233 rushing yards per game last year, it's a welcoming sign for Terps fans.

Amid the Terps' dominant ground game, Washington struggled to connect with his new receivers. The sophomore quarterback was errant on passes to Chris Durr Jr. and Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding during the opening drive, leading to the lone three-and-out.

Washington completed just four passes in the opening quarter for 15 yards, utilizing Williams out of the backfield as his top weapon. He had one catch for eight yards in the opening quarter and later connected with him for a 27-yard reception — Maryland's second-longest of the game.

But Washington settled in, showcasing the arm and leg talent that left fans in awe last year. On a 4th-and-4 play, Washington extended the play long enough to spot Durr open between several defenders. He threaded the needle to keep the drive going.

Washington linked up with Gladding on his next two completions during the drive, including a 10-yard reception at the back of the end zone for his lone passing touchdown of the game.

While he struggled to make the right reads with time in the pocket, Washington was at his best Saturday on the run. His added threat as a rusher — Washington scrambled three times, an element Maryland is looking to expand upon — further opened up receivers downfield.

Still, Washington's inaccuracies led to an underwhelming stat line. He went 19-of-31 for 186 passing yards, the second-fewest yards in his young career.

While the Terps returned just one piece from its starting defensive line last season, the pass rush wreaked havoc on Saturday.

Maryland consistently created pressure on Hampton quarterback Jalen Woods, totaling five sacks and forcing the inexperienced signal caller into some questionable decisions. He threw three picks, two of which sophomore safety Messiah Delhomme caught.

DD Holmes, who made just one start last season, was likely the Terps' best defensive player. He generated two of Maryland's five sacks and showcased his versatility on both the edge and interior of the line.

Hampton finished with only 10 rushing yards on its 31 attempts, and didn't fare any better through the air. The Pirates threw for 75 passing yards, with most coming after the game was already out of hand.

Maryland posted its first shutout since 2022 and allowed Hampton to get past midfield on just two of its drives. It never reached the red zone.

"Our defense did a tremendous job tackling. To have a shutout in the first game and create the turnovers and put the pressure on the quarterbacks, they did a great job," Locksley said.

articles.title: This is not about a clear and obvious error
articles.summary: The biggest issue with judging handball is often determining if the ball did actually hit the arm, and that is the crux of Nottingham Forest's argument.  Nec...
articles.body:
The biggest issue with judging handball is often determining if the ball did actually hit the arm, and that is the crux of Nottingham Forest's argument.

Neco Williams is adamant the ball came off his head and did not touch his hand, evidence which of course would not be available to the VAR.

Even having a chip in the ball, like at the World Cup, would not help here as the head and hands were so close together.

This is not about a clear and obvious error, as that covers subjective incidents like potential penalties.

It is a factual overturn so the VAR, Peter Bankes, is looking for definitive proof. This is similar but without taking into account what the referee, Craig Pawson, says he has seen.

Definitive proof can be seen as a higher bar than clear and obvious, because it is a factual decision - that the ball definitely touched the goalscorer's arm.

Oliver Glasner, Williams and most of the Forest fanbase refuse to accept that evidence does exist, and that there were no grounds to disallow the goal.

These decisions come down to one factor - the judgement of who is in the VAR room on a given match.

It is unavoidable that another VAR on a different day might feel the threshold of proof had not been crossed, and allow the goal to stand.

And this will always be one of the major frustrations with VAR.

Harry Maguire's goal against Ipswich last weekend was allowed despite a handball because his shot was going wide before it was deflected, meaning it was an own goal.

In Williams' case, he actually was the goalscorer so any touch on the arm means the goal must be ruled out.

The only thing that would have saved the goal was if the ball had fully crossed the line before it was kicked against Williams.

articles.title: Players will 'learn how we want them to play' - Maresca
articles.summary: Manchester City clung on to a nervy victory against the Sky Blues to maintain their 100% winning start to the season, but managed to get the job done courtes...
articles.body:
Manchester City clung on to a nervy victory against the Sky Blues to maintain their 100% winning start to the season, but managed to get the job done courtesy of a string of saves from goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Erling Haaland continued his fine start to the season by converting his third goal in as many games from Antoine Semenyo's deep cross, which came after Enzo Fernandez played through a slide-rule pass to the Ghanaian.

Playing in the number eight role, Argentina international Fernandez was given licence to roam and make late bursts into the box - he touched the ball six times in the opposition area, with only Haaland managing more with 11.

Fernandez could have had a dream debut but saw two shots blocked, before being replaced after 76 minutes by fellow summer signing Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international was part of City's midfield rebuild and highlights the options available to Enzo Maresca despite the departures of Bernardo Silva, Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez.

Iliman Ndiaye, meanwhile, became the first Senegalese player to represent City and is bound to give opposition defenders with his trickery and pace. No player attempted more dribbles in the match than his eight.

Maresca said: "Enzo and Iliman [played their] first game with us and then Ayyoub and Ryan [McAidoo] their first game in front of our fans.

"That is why I said there are many reasons I am happy about our win. I think they were all good.

"Ili just had two sessions with us. He needs to understand how to move. Most of the time he was moving in the wrong way, wrong position, but he needs to learn and for sure he is going to learn."

Asked to elaborate on Ndiaye's performance, Maresca said: "When Marc Guehi has the ball and he was dropping a lot and we don't need that.

"We need him in the last third so he can be a little bit more higher. That space was more for Josko Gvardiol.

"It is the same thing in this [other] side. But it is normal and with time they will learn the way we want them to play."

articles.title: BOUNCE BACK: Career night from Creel gets Jax State back on track
articles.summary: JACKSONVILLE — One week after picking themselves up off the turf in Fargo, the Jacksonville State Gamecocks found their rhythm — and then some. Behind a care...
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE — One week after picking themselves up off the turf in Fargo, the Jacksonville State Gamecocks found their rhythm — and then some.

Behind a career night from senior quarterback Caden Creel, Jax State exploded for 526 yards of offense to steamroll Eastern Kentucky 49-7 in Saturday night's home opener at AmFirst Stadium.

Creel set career highs with 21 completions, 327 passing yards and five touchdown passes in offensive coordinator Taylor Housewright's second game calling the plays.

"When guys execute, you can put up numbers like that and you can do things like that," Creel said. "Coach Housewright can call the plays that he called because we're executing. If we don't execute, then our offense is nothing."

The win provided a much-needed response from Creel and the Jax State offense after managing just 170 yards in a 33-7 season-opening loss to North Dakota State.

Creel said the Gamecocks "got punched in the mouth" in Fargo because of their lack of execution. They spent the week addressing those issues, and the improvement was evident Saturday night.

"This group is very resilient," Creel said. "Last week was a tough week, and the way that we bounced back this week, I think, was pretty impressive."

Jax State (1-1) wasted no time righting the ship, as Creel and fifth-year wide receiver Jamill Williams torched the defense on the Gamecocks' first three offensive possessions with touchdown passes of 13, 55 and 30 yards. Williams bounced back from a quiet 5-yard opener to finish with seven catches for 144 yards, capping his four-touchdown night with a 4-yard grab from Creel in the fourth quarter.

"He's one of the most competitive guys that I've been around," Jax State head coach Charles Kelly said when asked about Williams, a transfer from Division-II Albany State. "Even last week, even after the game, it was like, you know, this won't be the way it is."

Creel also completed a 24-yard touchdown pass to sophomore tight end Luke Gilbert to push the lead to 42-7 in the third quarter and finished second on the team with 54 rushing yards on 10 carries.

Junior running back Jalen Likely led the ground game with 73 yards on five carries — highlighted by a 45-yard touchdown run that made it 35-7 at halftime — though the Gamecocks did most of their damage through the air.

"They gave us some looks that we felt like we could take advantage of in the passing game, so I'm glad we were able to execute them," Kelly said.

Jax State's defense was equally dominant, holding Eastern Kentucky (0-2) to 285 yards of total offense. The lone blemish was a 72-yard touchdown run by Brady Hensley.

Fifth-year safety Caleb Nix picked up where he left off last season, intercepting Tyler Travers and returning it 43 yards for a second-quarter touchdown.

"He knows exactly what to do, where to be," said Jax State linebacker Walker O'Steen. "He's kind of like a coach on the field. He just does what he's supposed to do, and when you do that, you make plays."

O'Steen, a former White Plains standout, led the Gamecocks with eight tackles, while true freshman Ty Sims, a Gadsden City graduate, recorded his first career interception.

Jax State will now head to Athens, Ohio, to face the Ohio Bobcats, and the Gamecocks will do so with plenty of momentum on their side.

"I'm just excited to grow on it," Creel said. "We can't be content about what we did tonight. We've got to keep on wanting to do more and strive to be great."
authors: Jared Gravette, The Anniston Star, Ala.

articles.summary: Alpine's Pierre Gasly took a surprising first pole position of his F1 career in Monza, Italy. Here's the full starting grid with penalties applied.
articles.body:
Pierre Gasly delivered a stunning performance in Saturday's qualifying , putting his Alpine on pole position for the Italian Grand Prix in Monza.

The Frenchman clocked a lap time of 1m 21.786s on his final run, enough to launch to the top of the timesheets and secure his and the Enstone outfit's first-ever pole.

If the 30-year-old managed to convert the advantage into a victory, it would mark his second career win - the first being at this very venue back in 2020 when he drove for AlphaTauri (now Racing Bulls).

The victory would also represent Alpine's second ever following Esteban Ocon's triumph in Hungary in 2021.

George Russell 's Mercedes clocked in the second-fastest time at the Temple of Spee, falling short of pole by a mere 0.060s.

Oscar Piastri initially landed his McLaren in third place but was later handed a three-place grid penalty for impeding Liam Lawson during qualifying, which bumped him down to P6.

The penalty moved Ferrari's Charles Leclerc up to third on the grid, while teammate Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen of Red Bull will start from fourth and fifth respectively.

Franco Colapinto secured P7 in the other Alpine ahead of defending champion Lando Norris of McLaren, with Arvid Lindblad and Gabriel Bortoleto rounding out the fastest 10.

Elsewhere, current championship leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli had initially posted the seventh-fastest time for Mercedes but was pushed to the back of the grid due to an engine penalty, having exceeded the limit of four power units allowed in a season. He will be starting the race from 19th place.

Alexander Albon also received a heavy grid penalty for power unit changes which sees him start from 20th.

Meanwhile, Fernando Alonso of Aston Martin is set to start from the pit lane after taking new power unit components. Lawson, who was set to start from 21st after receiving a grid penalty for power unit changes, will also be sent to the pit lane after Red Bull changed his rear wing assembly.

Lawson continues to step in for Isack Hadjar, who has been sidelined for two races due to a wrist injury he sustained during the summer break.

Yuki Tsunoda temporarily fills in Lawson's seat at Racing Bulls.

Here's the starting order for Sunday's race in Monza with penalties applied:

Andrea Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes): +0.307

The Italian Grand Prix race starts at 3 p.m. local time (CEST) on Sunday, September 6.

articles.title: Rubens Barrichello reunites with Ferrari F2002 in Michael Schumacher’s honour
articles.summary: Rubens Barrichello took his and Michael Schumacher’s F2002 out for a drive as part of Ferrari’s celebrating the German at the Formula 1 2026 Italian Grand Pr...
articles.body:
Rubens Barrichello took his and Michael Schumacher's F2002 out for a drive as part of Ferrari's celebrating the German at the Formula 1 2026 Italian Grand Prix.

In celebration of Schumacher, his former teammate Barrichello got to drive the F2002 machinery again at Monza on Saturday afternoon after exhilarating F1 Italian GP qualifying, which saw a surprise pole from Alpine's Pierre Gasly – an underdog in the circumstances.

Before Sebastian Vettel's chance on Sunday pre-race, Barrichello got back in the car in which he won four races during the 2002 F1 season – including the Italian GP at Monza. The car saw 15 wins in the season, which sealed the constructors' title for Ferrari and drivers' for Schumacher.

Barrichello finished the season second to Schumacher with four wins and 10 podiums. Ferrari used sustainable fuel in the V8-powered car – prepared by Shell – as is the norm in current times. The F2002 is on display at Monza along with Schumacher's first Ferrari F310 from 1996 season and his last 248 from 2006.

There is also a special livery that Ferrari is running in F1 Italian GP weekend in honour of Schumacher, with both Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc sporting race suits with seven stars inscribed to denote the German's seven F1 world championships.

Barrichello wears his son's helmet for the run

The Brazilian wore the racing helmet of his son during the demonstration event. The youngster is currently racing in the FIA Formula 3 Championship with AIX Racing. "Fernando, my son. Taking your helmet for a "ride" in the Ferrari at 350 km/h was yet another huge thrill. I love you," Barrichello wrote.

Ferrari shared handful of videos from the special run undertaken by Barrichello on Saturday afternoon. Naturally, the V8 created lot of attention in the paddock and also among fans – a lot of them are new to the screaming engine noise.
